A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same context-length scaling research despite the changed title and organization. All 30 pages of v3 and 36 pages of v4, including appendices, equations, tables and figures, support comparison.

before.justification: v3 reports original OpenWebText training experiments, Llama loss and representation measurements, and synthetic parity experiments, including the model-versus-Bayes losses in Table 1.

after.justification: v4 retains original language-model and synthetic results and adds RULER accuracy experiments, position-weighted document QA, and entropy measurements on additional model families.

M1.justification: Intrinsic entropy, Gaussian-KDE and eigenvalue estimation, and the Transformer and MLP synthetic models already appear in v3, including Appendix B. v4 promotes and reapplies these components; the PDFs do not establish a changed proposed architecture, training algorithm or inference technique.

E1.justification: v4 adds downstream evaluation on RULER document QA, frequent-word extraction, common-word extraction and variable tracking, plus position-weighted QA using SQuAD paragraphs. These substantially extend task requirements beyond v3's language-loss and synthetic studies. The synthetic experiment reframed as two-needle training in Appendix F retains earlier coverage.

E2.justification: The Bayes-model and random-guess references and the KDE/PCA estimation comparisons are retained. No competing context-scaling method is newly evaluated against the proposed analysis. Qwen3 and RecurrentGemma serve as additional experimental models for testing generality.

E3.justification: The added downstream experiments introduce accuracy evaluation with fixed pretrained models, varying visible-context fractions, position-dependent query sampling, and 8k/16k maximum contexts. Appendix A specifies non-thinking Qwen3 configurations spanning 4B–32B. These are substantial new evaluation protocols; the retained OpenWebText training settings remain unchanged. Appendix A.1's 16k uniform-QA description conflicts with Figure 4's 8192-token label.

E4.justification: v4 adds analyses of query-position weighting, model size, maximum task length and architecture dependence, including RecurrentGemma outliers and the contrasting variable-tracking behavior. It also removes the Transformer experiment's CE-versus-thresholded-ID correlation panel from v3 Figure 11. Earlier Llama threshold sweeps and MLP analyses remain in the appendices.

E5.justification: v4 introduces an explicit regression exclusion practice: three high-loss RecurrentGemma observations are omitted from the fit in Figure 2 and Appendix G. Existing fit-parameter uncertainties are retained. Neither version documents experimental seeds or repeated-run uncertainty estimates.

E6.justification: v4 adds downstream accuracy curves showing interior optima in several QA/extraction settings, while variable-tracking accuracy increases throughout the tested range. Figure 2 reports new CE–KDE correlations of -0.9960 for Qwen3-8B-Base and -0.9967 for RecurrentGemma after exclusions. Table 1 and the earlier power-law fits are retained; the Transformer ID-correlation results are removed.

T1.justification: The four appendix theorems, proofs, and entropy/dimension assumptions are retained. Section 3 replaces v3's explicit dataset-size stationarity calculation with a task/model-parameterized argument covering training and inference, invoking convex Bayes risk and increasing inference approximation loss. v4 also explicitly assumes a differentiable extension of integer context length.

C1.justification: v4 makes intrinsic entropy the central named contribution and broadens the principal optimal-context claim from training-data dependence to fixed-model downstream inference and task context requirements. This changes the claimed scope in the introduction and conclusion, although the entropy framework itself already existed in v3's appendix.

C2.justification: v4 adds substantive explanations of task-dependent and model-dependent optima, variable-tracking behavior, and RecurrentGemma's failure to approximate Bayes risk at short contexts. It qualifies entropy as an imperfect QA-accuracy proxy. v3's explicit limitation concerning short-context pretraining followed by long-context training is omitted.

D1.justification: v4 adds RULER construction, truncation and inference-mode instructions, but drops v3 Appendix E's explicit synthetic bit-pair construction and Appendix F.2's detailed MLP architecture, optimizer, sample counts and training settings. Those MLP results remain in Appendices F and K, so this substantially reduces their reproducibility documentation. The experiment-code URL is unchanged.

R1.justification: v4 adds citations including RULER, SQuAD and Qwen3, while most related-work discussion remains stable. Chen et al.'s L2M remains cited, but v3's substantive explanation of its complementary hidden-state bound and independent concurrency is removed. Its publication update alone is bibliographic.

P1.justification: v4 retitles the paper, substantially rewrites the introduction and conclusion, centers the main narrative on entropy, and reorganizes the synthetic and theoretical explanations across appendices. The Transformer study moves into the main text, dimension/MLP material moves to Appendix K, and training and downstream inference receive separate treatment.

P2.justification: Figure 1 is rebuilt around a decomposition schematic, retained training results and downstream errors. v4 adds multi-model entropy plots, a position-weighted QA diagram and downstream sensitivity plots. Numerous existing figures move, and v3's four-panel Transformer Figure 11 becomes the two-panel Figure 7. Captions and document layout also change substantially.

improvement.justification: The new downstream accuracy experiments and cross-architecture entropy measurements strengthen the connection between the framework and practical model behavior, including informative exceptions in Figures 2, 4 and 8. The entropy-centered narrative also improves accessibility. These gains are tempered by removal of reproducibility details for retained synthetic experiments and inconsistent context-length descriptions in the new QA evaluation, yielding a useful but limited net improvement.
